result.Method of Attack: Encrypts files on compromised Microsoft Windows machines and demands ransom for file decryption; terminates specific processes and stops services before encrypting files; appends specific file extensions to encrypted files (.dark_power for Dark Power, .PayMe100USD for PayMe100USD); drops ransom notes demanding cryptocurrency payment (Monero for Dark Power, Bitcoin for PayMe100USD); claims data theft and threatens to publish stolen data if ransom is not paid
result.Attack Vector: Unknown for Dark Power but likely similar to other ransomware groups; fake Bing installers for PayMe100USD (disguised as 'newbing.exe')
result.Indicators of Compromise: File hashes: 33c5b4c9a6c24729bb10165e34ae1cd2315cfce5763e65167bd58a57fde9a389 (Dark Power), 11ddebd9b22a3a21be11908feda0ea1e1aa97bc67b2dfefe766fcea467367394 (Dark Power), c2aa5d89d1fb63c65806a789f529daf774ceff411338c43438ea6c0175e10fd0 (PayMe100USD), 4daca38854ba0a471d25250f106122ff81b8bbda2b19569a9e0b6e7f56187746 (PayMe100USD); ransom note files: readme.pdf (Dark Power), PayMe 1.txt to PayMe 8.txt (PayMe100USD); executable file names: ef.exe (Dark Power), newbing.exe (PayMe100USD)
